title: Observe Agent Quality, Cost, and Risk
summary: Instrument agent runs with privacy-preserving traces, metrics, logs, and quality signals that support diagnosis without turning telemetry into a sensitive-data archive.
objectives: Design traces that connect agent, model, retrieval, tool, approval, handoff, and verification spans.
Measure quality, safety, reliability, latency, token use, cost, and escalation by meaningful slices.

Use traces to localize failure and route human escalation without exposing hidden reasoning.

sections.title: Use traces, metrics, logs, and evaluations together
paragraphs: A trace reconstructs one run and its parent-child operations. Metrics reveal trends and service objectives. Logs capture discrete operational events. Evaluations judge behavior against a rubric. None replaces the others. activity.title: Instrument and review an agent trace
instructions: Create a trace schema for one workflow with agent, model, retrieval, tool, approval, handoff, verification, and recovery spans.
Define quality, safety, reliability, latency, token, cost, and escalation metrics with dimensions and alert thresholds.
Write the telemetry data policy covering collection purpose, redaction, content capture, sampling, access, retention, deletion, and residency.
Review one synthetic failed trace, identify the first wrong transition, assign a failure class, and prepare a human-escalation packet.
evidence: A trace/span schema, metric catalog, service objectives, and alert rules tied to product decisions.
A privacy policy and trace-review artifact showing causal diagnosis, failure classification, containment status, and escalation evidence.

questions.prompt: Which signal best reconstructs the causal sequence of one agent run?
questions.explanation: A trace preserves parent-child operations and timing for an individual run.

questions.prompt: What is a better cost metric than total tokens alone?
choices: Cost per verified successful task, segmented by workflow
questions.explanation: Cost must be related to useful outcomes to guide product decisions.

questions.prompt: How should raw model and tool content be handled in telemetry?
choices: Default to minimization and secure references; capture only under explicit policy
questions.explanation: Agent content can contain sensitive data and requires purpose, access, retention, and deletion controls.

questions.prompt: Where should trace diagnosis begin after a user-visible failure?
choices: Walk backward to the first transition that violated its expected contract
questions.explanation: The first causal divergence may be earlier and at a different system boundary than the visible symptom.

questions.prompt: What belongs in a human escalation packet?
choices: A redacted timeline, affected targets, containment, evidence, and required decision
questions.explanation: The human needs decision-ready evidence without unnecessary sensitive content.
